newsitem.title: UK: Bradford & Bingley to stay building society.
newsitem.headline: Bradford & Bingley to stay building society.

text.p: - Britain's Bradford & Bingley on Monday said it was financially and strategically committed to remain a mutually owned building society.
"We can't see why other building societies did it," Chief Executive Christopher Rodrigues told Reuters, referring to the recent trend among building societies to stock market flotations.
He said the company, a medium-sized society with 17 billion sterling in assets at the end of 1996, would be best served if it remained a niche player.
It would not follow in the footsteps of the Halifax, due to float on the London stock exchange in June, and other recent building society flotations.
"I think it is nice to be different. It helps you stand out from the crowd," he said.
The advantage of being mutual was not having shareholders pushing for dividends and diversification, he said.
"You can go and have your equity fund somewhere else," the chief executive said of potential shareholders.

Bradford & Bingley posted profit after tax for 1996 of 56.6 million sterling, down from 107.7 million in 1995 because of increased benefits to its members, a 20 million sterling reorganisation charge and adoption of more conservative accounting.

Since Bradford & Bingley reaffirmed its mutuality last year, new account openings have close to doubled. But he said the company was not worried about investors hoping to make a quick profit gambling on a possible public flotation.
"Carpetbaggers will be very disappointed if they are looking for a dividend," Rodrigues said.
With 900 million sterling in reserves, the company would remain open-minded to growth by asset acquisitions, Rodrigues.
"Strategically there are certain bits of the business that would make sense for us to gain scale in quickly," he said without giving any details of possible acquisitions.
He said the company would focus on its core mortgage-lending and savings account business.
